headline: Skyward gets its runway
lede: Gullwing Isle gains the second landing strip — a painted, zone-scored runway on the south beach, so every glider sortie now ends with a choice: the precision of the bullseye or the nerve of carrying it deep.

notes.text: SKYWARD's glider can now land on a real runway: touch down soft and straight and the score depends on how far down the strip you carry it — SHORT 150, MIDDLE 300, LONG 450, FULL STRIP 700. Crab in past ~17° and it's a scuff; the bullseye's 1000 stays the precision prize.
The strip is honest engineering: scoring laws are pure in sim.js, the replay hash never felt it, and the autopilot still aims at the mat — five-seed pins prove the graduation line is untouched.
skywardcheck grew 17 pins and four new mutants (all 30 die); the live browser drive lands FULL STRIP +700 on a wind-crabbed short-final with zero console errors.

A 14 m strip and ±2.2 m/s of seed wind is the lesson: single-tick Node pins never feel drift — it takes a multi-second live leg to catch it. Drive legs fly short finals, crabbed to a straight ground track.
